title: REAL A(M, N) — explicit-shape array; column-major iteration is required for cache locality
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE FILL_MATRIX(A, M, N)
C     Fortran arrays are column-major. The inner loop varies the
C     LEFT subscript so consecutive iterations touch consecutive
C     memory addresses. Reversing the loop order (I outer, J inner)
C     leaves the code correct but cache-thrashes for large N.
C     Java/C# arrays are row-major -- the natural loop order
C     reverses too. A port that preserves the F77 loop order on a
C     row-major target silently turns a fast inner loop into a slow
C     outer one.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER M, N, I, J
      REAL    A(M, N)
      DO J = 1, N
         DO I = 1, M
            A(I, J) = REAL(I + J)
         END DO
      END DO
      END
notes: Fortran's column-major layout is one of the few places where translating loop order matters for correctness-via-performance. A naive Java port that keeps J-outer/I-inner on a 2D array works but is 5-10x slower on large matrices. The spec should capture the column-major dependency AND ask whether the rewrite should preserve loop order or rewrite for the target's layout.
